explanation: An atomicity violation is a concurrency bug in which a sequence of instructions intended to execute as a single, indivisible unit is interrupted by another thread, leading to inconsistent program states. It is important to understand this concept to identify and prevent errors in multi-threaded C programs, ensuring data integrity and reliability in concurrent environments.
example_explanation: This example creates two threads that each increment a shared variable without synchronization. The increment operation is not atomic, so an atomicity violation may occur if one thread interrupts the other, potentially resulting in an incorrect final value for shared_var, thus illustrating how such violations lead to unpredictable behavior in concurrent programs.
